appium-uiautomator2-driver chain (HIGH: shell-quote GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv via @appium/support + @appium/base-driver; LOW: body-parser GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6): RESOLVED 2026-08-03 — no longer an accepted residual. The evidence is the resolved tree, not a release number: a fresh npm install --package-lock-only from origin/main @ 01381d96, run in a scratch dir, resolves the nested subtree to @appium/support 7.2.6 -> shell-quote 1.10.0 and @appium/base-driver 10.7.2 -> body-parser 2.3.0, and that resolve is byte-identical to the committed lockfile, so it is main's real state and not a scratch artifact. npm audit now reports 0 critical / 0 high / 0 moderate and lists none of shell-quote, body-parser, @appium/support or @appium/base-driver as an advisory root (the remaining 18 low are the separate elliptic chain). NOTE THE SHAPE OF THE FIX — the old revisit trigger ("the nested node_modules/appium-uiautomator2-driver/node_modules/@appium/support key disappears") NEVER FIRED and was the wrong trigger: the 257-package duplicate subtree is still there, it just now duplicates PATCHED copies. Nothing was remediated deliberately; the subtree was re-resolved as a side effect of routine lockfile regeneration on 2026-07-29 — it flipped to 1.10.0 at 87e9897b (npm-minor-patch group, #1465, 07:49), regressed to 1.8.4 at ff78ac99 (i18n Phase 1 lockfile, 08:01), and was restored at 0295fd40 (regenerate package-lock.json to match package.json, 08:56), holding at 1.10.0 across every lockfile commit since. Route (4) of the four previously-failed remediations — delete the nested entries and re-resolve, npm re-derives them byte-identically at the old versions — no longer holds, because the nested ranges (appium-adb ^7.2.2, appium-android-driver ^7.2.5, teen_process ^1.8.1, express ^2.2.1) now resolve to the patched versions. The 2026-07-27 lesson stands and is exactly why this retirement is written around a lockfile diff rather than an upstream release: a version number is not evidence, npm fixAvailable is not evidence, only the resolved tree is. That entry was retired once on a version-number trigger and had to be reinstated the same day; if you are reading this while considering a similar retirement elsewhere, reproduce the resolve first. WATCHER: this note claimed 'veyrnox-appium-shellquote-watch deleted 2026-08-03 by the run that produced this note'. That was NOT true — the watcher was still registered and enabled on 2026-08-23, three weeks later, and had in fact never run once (no lastRunAt at all). Corrected here rather than reworded, because the false claim is the interesting part: this note recorded the chain as RESOLVED on 2026-08-03 while .claude/scheduled-tasks/veyrnox-daily-dep-audit/SKILL.md kept both entries under '## Accepted residuals' until 2026-08-23, so each file described a different state for three weeks and a reader of either one had no way to know. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-23 by a manual run of that watcher at origin/main 8b3d3fb: fresh npm install --package-lock-only resolves the nested subtree to @appium/support 7.2.6 -> shell-quote 1.10.0 and @appium/base-driver 10.7.2 -> body-parser 2.3.0 (257 nested entries, node_modules/appium 3.6.0 present so the resolve is sound), and npm audit reports 22 low / 0 moderate / 0 high / 0 critical with elliptic as the sole advisory root and none of the four packages appearing. The low count is 22 rather than the 18 stated earlier in this note because the separate elliptic chain grew when @keystonehq/keystone-sdk was added, not because anything here regressed. Deleting the watcher is recommended to the owner; the run that produced this note may not delete scheduled tasks itself. Dependabot alerts #12 and #14 should resolve. NOT VERIFIED: the e2e-emulator CI job has not been re-run since the subtree moved — the Android E2E harness's entire dependency tree changed underneath it as a side effect, with no deliberate test. If that harness starts failing, look here first.

brace-expansion GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (HIGH: DoS via unbounded expansion length causing an out-of-memory process crash): RESOLVED 2026-08-02 via PR #1537 — no longer an accepted residual, and NO overrides entry was needed or added. Upstream BACKPORTED the DoS fix to both old-shape lines (2.1.3 published 2026-07-28, 1.1.17 published 2026-07-29; newest now 1.1.18 / 2.1.4), so the existing declared ranges ^1.1.7 / ^2.0.1 / ^2.0.2 simply resolve to patched versions on their own. Fresh npm install --package-lock-only from origin/main @ 01381d96 gives brace-expansion 1.1.17, 2.1.3 and 5.0.8 — every copy patched — and npm audit reports 0 critical / 0 high / 0 moderate with brace-expansion absent from the advisory roots entirely (the remaining 18 low are the separate elliptic chain). This is exactly the revisit trigger the previous note specified ("OR if upstream backports the fix to the 1.x/2.x lines"), which fired as designed on 2026-08-03. KEEP THIS PART — THE 5.x HAZARD IS UNCHANGED AND STILL LIVE: brace-expansion 5.x exports an OBJECT { expand } from dist/commonjs while 1.x and 2.x do module.exports = expand (a bare function), so an overrides entry of ^5.0.8 / ^5.x still throws TypeError: expand is not a function at node_modules/minimatch/minimatch.js braceExpand on first use. Re-probed 2026-08-03 against the then-latest 5.0.9: still an object, still throws. Six of the nine minimatch copies still declare old-shape ranges (root 3.1.5 ^1.1.7; mocha/filelist/webdriverio 5.1.9 ^2.0.1; @wdio/config/archiver-utils 9.0.9 ^2.0.2), so that override would still break lint and the obfuscator step. Do NOT reach for a 5.x override to "consolidate" these copies. The backports are safe precisely because they preserve the bare-function export — verified functionally on 2026-08-03, not inferred from the version: 1.1.17 and 2.1.3 each report typeof function and each let require('minimatch')('abd','a{b,c}d') return true. HOW IT LANDED, including the trap it hit: the first attempt (87fe8fd2) ran npm audit fix --legacy-peer-deps and rewrote the lockfile -4582/+1918, stripping the appium subtree — the documented --legacy-peer-deps hazard, hit again. Corrected by 5d9c9a17 ("use targeted lockfile patch instead of full --legacy-peer-deps rewrite"), which is fully green including lint-and-build (the acceptance test that matters here — npm run build passes even when the export shape is broken, so it is NOT evidence) and e2e-emulator-tests (31, google_apis). WATCHER RETIRED: veyrnox-brace-expansion-watch deleted 2026-08-03 by the run that produced this note. If brace-expansion ever regresses it will surface as a normal unsuppressed npm audit finding, which is the correct default.

brace-expansion GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 (HIGH: DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays, bypassing the CVE-2026-14257 mitigation — this is a NEW advisory, distinct from GHSA-mh99 above, affecting the SAME version numbers that GHSA-mh99 had cleared: <=1.1.17, 2.0.0-2.1.3, 4.0.0-5.0.8) + undici GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272 (HIGH: cross-user info disclosure/parse-time crash via degenerate private cache directives): found 2026-08-10 by the weekly dep-audit. `npm audit fix --package-lock-only` (targeted, not --force, not a full regeneration — small diff) cleared 7 of 8 vulnerable copies on its own, all within existing declared ranges, no package.json change: node_modules/undici 7.28.0→7.29.0 (root), node_modules/@vercel/blob/node_modules/undici 6.27.0→6.28.0, and six brace-expansion copies (root 1.1.17→1.1.18, archiver-utils/mocha/webdriverio 2.1.3→2.1.4, glob/readdir-glob 5.0.8→5.0.9). It left node_modules/appium-uiautomator2-driver/node_modules/brace-expansion at 5.0.8 untouched for unclear reasons (declared range there is ^5.0.8, which 5.0.9 satisfies fine) — hand-patched that one entry to 5.0.9 directly. NO overrides entry was needed or added for any of the 8, matching the precedent above. Side effects of the audit-fix re-resolution, both harmless: added utf-8-validate entries under @walletconnect/core and jayson (fixes a pre-existing lockfile/package.json drift that was making a bare `npm ci` fail even on unmodified main — 'Missing: utf-8-validate@5.0.10 from lock file'), and collapsed a duplicate JSON key for node_modules/motion/node_modules/framer-motion (+motion-dom/motion-utils) that had two conflicting stanzas in the committed lockfile; npm (and any JSON parser) only ever honored the second one, so removing the dead first stanza changes nothing that was actually in effect. Verified: npm audit reports 0 critical/0 high (18 low, same pre-existing elliptic chain), npm ci passes cleanly against the resulting lockfile, lint clean, vite build succeeds.
